QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.claim: Transgressors exceed human nature’s balance toward animal or predatory ranks and prefer sensory pleasure to real life, so hell becomes their home.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.anchor: تعدى طور الفطرة الإنسانية وجاوز حد العدالة والشريعة إلى الرتبة البهيمية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.claim: The transgressor is one who disbelieves and prefers worldly life to the hereafter; Hell is his home.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.anchor: {فأما من طغى} في كفره. {وآثر الحياة الدنيا} على الآخرة. {فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه

NAHHAS:v5p146/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r7.claim: Man is nominative as the subject, with its predicate in the next clause.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r7.anchor: من في موضع رفع بالابتداء وخبره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.claim: Mujahid says the great calamity is when people are sent to Malik, guardian of Hell; ṭaghā means disobeyed, marsāhā means its time, and its mention means the Hour.
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فإذا جاءت الطامة}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.claim: Leaders prefer worldly life because, despite recognizing the Messenger's truth, they resent following another and losing their authority.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.anchor: فإن سادتهم ومسيريهم يعلمون أن ما يدعوهم إليه الرسول هو الحق ولكنهم يكرهون متابعته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.claim: طغى means crossing proper human limits through disbelief and preferring worldly life because of denying the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.anchor: طغى معناه: تجاوز الحدود التي ينبغي للإنسان أن يقف عندها بأن كفر وآثر الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.claim: The rebel is one who defies God and prefers worldly life over religion and the Hereafter; Hell is his destination, with food from zaqqum and drink of boiling water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.anchor: أي: تمرد وعتا، {وآثر الحياة الدنيا} أي: قدمها على أمر دينه وأخراه،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.claim: The response after فإذا is ‘then the matter is as follows’; الجحيم هي المأوى means Hell is his abode, with a known possessor understood rather than expressed, and هي is either a separator or subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.anchor: أي : فإذا جاءت الطاقة فإن الأمر كذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r1.claim: To transgress is to exceed the limit through disobedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r2.claim: The passage was revealed about al-Nadr and his son al-Harith, but applies generally to every disbeliever who prefers worldly life to the Hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r2.anchor: نزلت في النضر وابنه الحارث، وهي عامة في كل كافر

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r3.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r3.claim: A person who takes three dishes of one food has transgressed.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r3.anchor: من اتخذ من طعام واحد ثلاثة ألوان فقد طغى

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r4.speaker: حذيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r4.claim: Through Juwaybir from al-Dahhak, Hudhayfa says he most fears this community will prefer what it sees over what it knows.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r4.anchor: أخوف ما أخاف على هذه الأمة أن يؤثروا ما يرون على ما يعلمون

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r5.speaker: رواية في الكتب
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r5.claim: A report found in earlier books says God burdens a servant with worries and loss if the servant prefers worldly life to the next, then does not care how the servant perishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r5.anchor: لا يؤثر عبد لي دنياه على آخرته، إلا بثثت عليه همومه وضيعته

RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.claim: After describing Resurrection generally, God divides those morally responsible into wretched and blessed, beginning with the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.anchor: قسم المكلفين قسمين : الأشقياء والسعداء ، فذكر حال الأشقياء

STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī treats fear of standing before God as the opposite of rebellion: rebellion implies ignorance, while fear implies knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r2.anchor: Al-Rāzī sees this fear of standing before his Lord as the exact opposite of one who rebelled in v. 37

STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.claim: Forbidding caprice opposes preferring worldly life; fear of God leads to obedience and good deeds, while caprice leads astray.
STUDYQURAN:79:40/r3.anchor: one who forbids the soul from caprice is the opposite of one who prefers the life of this world

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.claim: The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.anchor: وقدم صفة أهل الجحيم لأن وجه الكلام إلى المشركين

TABRISI:79:45-46/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r5.claim: Transgression means crossing God's limits through sins, and preferring worldly life means choosing it over the Hereafter; Hell becomes the transgressor's refuge.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r5.anchor: أي تجاوز الحد الذي حده الله وارتكب المعاصي

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.claim: These brief verses summarize negative and positive attitudes that prepare either immense loss or salvation in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.anchor: Bu birkaç kısa âyette âhiretteki büyük kaybı veya büyük kurtuluşu hazırlayan olumsuz ve olumlu tutumların çok veciz bir özeti yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.claim: Ṭughyān is contrasted with hilm in al-Tur 52:33 and describes the impulsive, unthinking, stubborn, unbelieving attitude of pre-Islamic people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.anchor: “Azgınlık” diye çevirdiğimiz “tuğyân” kavramı Tûr sûresinde (52/33) “akıllı ve ağırbaşlı düşünüp davranma” mânasındaki “hilm”in karşıtı olarak kullanılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.claim: Such people usually live for the immediate moment and do not look beyond the transient world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.anchor: Böyleleri genellikle anlık yaşadıkları için fâni dünyanın ötesine bakmazlar

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the apodosis is the statement that Hell is the abode, with a compound condition: when the calamity comes, whoever arrives as a transgressor has Hell as his home.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.anchor: أن جوابه قوله : { فإن الجحيم هى المأوى } وكأنه جزاء مركب على شرطين

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r4.claim: Some identify the transgressor who prefers worldly life as al-Naḍr and his father al-Ḥārith.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r4.anchor: منهم من قال : المراد بقوله : { طغى * وءاثر الحيواة الدنيا }

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r5.claim: Rāzī allows the passage to have been occasioned by their misconduct but rejects restricting it to them: the wording and its operative trait are general.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r5.anchor: وإن كان المراد تخصيصها به ، فبعيد لأن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r6.claim: Transgression reflects corruption of the theoretical faculty: one who knows God recognizes his own insignificance and God's power, and therefore should not rebel.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r6.anchor: قوله صغى ، إشارة إلى فساد حال القوة النظرية

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.claim: Rāzī infers that the sinner who lacks these two defining traits is not described as having Hell for his permanent abode.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.anchor: وتخصيصه بهذه الحالة يدل على أن الفاسق الذي لا يكون كذلك ، لا تكون الجحيم مأوى له

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r1.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī reads rebellion as corruption of intellect: those who know God recognize their insignificance and do not incline toward arrogance.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r1.anchor: Al-Rāzī interprets one who rebels to indicate corruption of the intellect, for all who know God know their own insignificance

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.claim: Together, intellectual and practical corruption represent the greatest corruption and merit eternal punishment; Hell is the refuge for those reaching this level.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.anchor: The two together are thus taken to indicate the greatest degree of corruption, the punishment for which is eternal

TAB-FULL:v24p98/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p98/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p98/r1.claim: The transgressor is one who was arrogant toward his Lord, disobeyed Him, and was too proud to worship Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.claim: The person who transgresses and prefers worldly life is a disbeliever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {فأما من طغى (37) وآثر الحياة الدنيا} يعني الكافر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say the verses were revealed about al-Nadr and his father al-Harith.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬5)، والكلبي (¬6): نزلت في النضر وأبيه الحرث

SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.claim: Transgression means denying God’s rights and rejecting His blessings, while preferring worldly life by pursuing desires and passions.
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : جحد حقوق الله وكفر نعمه وآثر الحياة الدنيا اتباعا في طلب الشهوات

SULAMI:v2p371#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r2.claim: Junayd defines transgression as crossing the bounds of what is due.
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - : الطغيان تعدى الحقوق

SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.claim: Abu ʿUthman defines transgression as turning away from the afterlife and turning toward worldly life.
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : الطغيان الإعراض عن الآخرة والإقبال على الدنيا

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r1.claim: The one who transgresses denies God's rights and rejects His blessing.

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.claim: Everyone is ignorant except the one who prefers God over self, spirit, this world, and the afterlife.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.anchor: ما طلعت شمس ولا غربت على أحد إلا وهو جاهل، إلا من يؤثر الله تعالى على نفسه وروحه ودنياه وآخرته

NASHR:v2p81/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r2.speaker: البصري والشامي والكوفي
NASHR:v2p81/r2.claim: The Basran, Syrian, and Kufan counters count فأما من طغى as an āya ending; the two Medinan counters and the Meccan do not.
NASHR:v2p81/r2.anchor: في النازعات فأما من طغى عدها البصري، والشامي، والكوفي، ولم يعدها المدنيان

NASHR:v2p81/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r8.speaker: الأزرق عن ورش
NASHR:v2p81/r8.claim: Al-Azraq’s Warsh routes through Ibn Ghalbūn and others open these non-final forms; al-Taysīr and related routes read them between vowels because they are written with yāʾ, including فأما من طغى.
NASHR:v2p81/r8.anchor: والأزرق عن ورش يفتح جميعه أيضا من طريق أبي الحسن بن غلبون، وأبيه عبد المنعم ومكي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers taking the response to إذا as the clause beginning فأما; Alusi considers this sound and says the syntax is straightforward if the preceding clause is conditional.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.anchor: جواب إذا على أنها شرطية لا ظرفية كما جوز على طريقة قوله تعالى فأما يأتينكم مني هدى الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.claim: Alternatively, the response to إذا is omitted and the تفصيل clause explains it; other suggestions derive the omission from what precedes or follows, which Alusi finds unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.anchor: وقيل جوابها محذوف كأنه قيل فإذا جاءت وقع ما لا يدخل تحت الوصف وقوله سبحانه فأما الخ تفصيل لذلك المحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r3.claim: The one who transgressed is one who rebelled against obedience and exceeded the bounds in disobedience until unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r3.anchor: أي فأما من عنا وتمرد عن الطاعة وجاوز الحد في العصيان حتى كفر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r1.claim: The preceding reference to those who do not hear Hell's faintest sound is linked to the statement in al-Anbiyaʾ 21:102.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r1.anchor: الأنبياء : 102 ] . ولما كان جواب ( إذا ) كما مضى محذوفا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r2.claim: The answer to the conditional when-clause is omitted; the author supplies the sense that people are divided into two groups, one destined for Hell and one for bliss.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r2.anchor: وكان تقديره أن قسم الناس قسمين : قسم للجحيم وقسم للنعيم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r3.claim: The transgressor exceeds the bounds of aggression and does not fear standing before his Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r3.anchor: أي تجاوز الحد في العدوان فلم يخش مقام ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r4.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r4.claim: Al-Qamus says ṭaghā means exceeding the measure or rising; it can also mean disbelief, excess in sins and oppression, and is used of rising water.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p319/r4.anchor: قال في القاموس : طغى : جاوز القدر وارتفع وطغى : إلا في الكفر وأسرف في المعاصي والظلم , والماء : ارتفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r1.claim: The division that follows details the prior clause; a thing cannot coherently be branched from itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r1.anchor: ومناط التفريع هو ما عقبه من التفصيل بقوله : { فأما من طغى } الخ إذ لا يلتئم تفريع الشيء على نفسه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r3.claim: The fāʾ links the nominal clause ‘as for whoever transgressed’ as the response to idhā; in meaning idhā governs the predicative relation between subject and predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r3.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فأما من طغى } رابطة لجواب ( إذا ) لأن جملة { من طغى } إلى آخرها جملة اسمية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r4.claim: Ammā marks division and condition, with the sense ‘whatever may occur’.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r4.anchor: و ( أما ) حرف تفصيل وشرط لأنها في معنى : مهما يكن شيء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r5.claim: Here transgression means transgressing God’s command, as the contrast with fearing one’s Lord’s station shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r5.anchor: والطغيان تقدم معناه آنفا . والمراد هنا : طغى على أمر الله ، كما دل عليه قوله : { وأما من خاف مقام ربه } .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#3/r1.claim: The person who transgressed is one who persisted in disbelief.

MUJAHID:v2p728#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p728#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p728#3/r1.claim: Mujahid explains transgression here as disobedience.
MUJAHID:v2p728#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ فأما من طغى ﴾ يعني من عصى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r1.claim: “As for” answers the earlier “when”; when the overwhelming calamity comes, the matter is as described.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r1.anchor: جواب فإذا أى إذا جاءت الطامة فإن الأمر كذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#15/r2.claim: The transgressor is one who crosses the limit and disbelieves.
